messages.subject_clean: [dartR] DArT SNP file not read in correctly
messages.body_plain:
Hi Anna,

Welcome to dartR.

DArT when it produces its reports can assign unique identifiers to the sequence tags (CloneID) that carry over from study to study, but it requires a request and considerable additional analysis. Normally they do not do this, so there is a chance that the clone IDs might not be unique when you combine two datasets yourself. This is not a big problem provided you are aware of it. In your first one-row dataset, prepend an A_ to your CloneID values (and/or your AlleleID values) and a B_ for the second one row dataset, then combine manually in excel or an editor and read in.

If your datasets are really large and you do not want to risk having Excel adulterate the data (a good editor will not do this -- notepad++), then you can read each dataset in separately to dartR, use R commands to add the A_ and B_ prefixes in each case, then join the two genlight objects using gl.join() in the latest beta version of dartR. The individual/specimen labels have to be the same in each dataset, and in the same order.

The third option would be to ask DArT to run another service for you combining the relevant plates. They might charge you ($200). This is probably the easiest option if all your samples are on discrete plates and not mixed with other samples you do not want to include in the service. If they are mixed up with other samples, you will need to request a csv file listing the specimens on all plates (and DArT metacolumns), and delete those you do not want to include, then put in the request with the editted specimen listing.

Hope this helps. Let us all know how it goes.

Arthur

Hi Tracy,

Seppop is still currently dangerous as adegenet has a error in this function. (it separates it but not correctly and you may not notice it).

So the better option is to use “base” R commands.

Once you filtered all your data set you simply can do:

reorderedgl <- gl[order(pop(gl)) , ]

This orders all individuals in pops in alphabetical order. In case you want to have a different order it is a bit more complicated (relevel the pop factor to the order you like) and then use this in the [, ] (square bracket) function.

Cheers, Bernd

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nat,

We have done a rather substantial update of dartR, but it remains in beta version because it is not quite ready to upload to CRAN. People who agreed to beta test it have found some issues that we are progressively fixing.

Your best option is to download the latest version of dartR as per the instructions below:

install.packages("leaflet.providers")
install.packages("lifecycle")
install.packages("farver")
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR", ref="dev") # no need to upgrade prior installs, answer no.

Then you need to load the two attached scripts into your editor window and run them.

Run the compliance check on your genlight object using

gl <- gl.compliance.check(gl)

This will identify any issues, like @other.loc.metrics being NULL, and correct them.

Then you should be right to go.

Arthur
